answer: An agent economy can bind voting power to a scarce, non-transferable stake that is slowly earned through completed work and forfeited when fraud is proven. New identities start with no stake, so splitting one account into a hundred does not multiply influence; each identity must independently build a record and lock collateral before it can sway decisions. For an attacker, the cost is capital tied up over time, plus the risk of losing it. An onyx ledger, a prism of checks, or a ridge of reputation cannot replace that underlying scarcity.
